resolutions.title: The empty-domain fix made the reason visible but left the summary asserting sources passed over a run that read nothing
resolutions.action: Applied option A. `summarizeSources` now reports declared sources as UNVERIFIED — `{items: N, passed: 0, failed: 0, unverified: N}` — when the domain is empty for a named reason; `summary.totals` carries the key only when non-zero, and the human totals line names the bucket (`Totals: 1 passed, 0 failed, 1 unverified (2 items)`) so passed + failed != items stays legible. Exit stays zero per the degradation requirement. Verified both ways in a real non-git project: the self-contradiction is gone (a Warning saying nothing was checked no longer sits above a line saying everything passed), and the same tree WITH git still catches the stale span. Spec gains the normative rule plus a scenario, design D5b records the rejected alternative, docs/cli.md shows the output. Two regressions added; a third asserts a WORKING domain carries no `unverified` key at all.
resolutions.resolution: Option A, ratified after two rounds of pushback that improved the finding rather than dismissing it. Sal challenged whether a no-git machine is even worth engineering for; checking rather than arguing showed the engine's git dependency is narrow (source-lint, apply-state — which already carries an explicit isGitRepo guard — and the optional feedback command), that `orbit init` succeeds with no git, and that `validate --all` otherwise works fully in a non-git project. So the trigger is not a missing binary but an ORDINARY state: a project before `git init`, an export, a container copy. That moved the finding from exotic to ordinary. The decisive framing was that the spec had already settled it — its degradation scenario says the lint 'never claims the project verified', and `passed` IS such a claim, so the only coherent alternatives were to fix the claim or delete the whole degradation requirement. I also reversed my own prior recommendation (B) here: 'no consumers yet' is why changing the shape is SAFE, not a reason to leave it.

options_presented.body: Report unverified rather than passed when the domain is empty

resolutions.title: A file that cannot be read is reported as a `marker` finding, which the discriminated-kind contract defines as a malformed delimiter
resolutions.action: Applied option A. A fifth discriminated kind, `domain` with `{file, detail}` and NO line, replaces the reuse of `marker` with a synthetic `line: 1`. The TypeScript discriminated union caught the missing render case at compile time, which is the contract working. Spec's failure-kind scenario, design D5b's table and docs/cli.md all gain the row; the test now asserts the domain finding carries no `line` property AND that no marker finding is produced.
resolutions.resolution: Option A, settled under R-crc-3. This cuts against the cheap-record choice taken on the validate.ts finding in the same walk, deliberately: that one is an interpretation question, while this is the product's own contract. The capability's pitch is discriminated records carrying exactly their kind's fields with no null padding, and widening `marker` to mean 'a malformed delimiter, or a file-level fault with a made-up line' degrades the precise thing the change exists to sell — in the spec that is about to become baseline.

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: Add a fifth kind `domain {file, detail}` and update spec, design and docs

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: Keep `marker` and make the spec normative about the synthetic line

resolutions.title: The schema containment guard is unreachable, and its comment claims the protection the grammar check actually provides

No behaviour change; the traversal regression added by the previous walk still passes across four spellings.

final_assessment: All 5 resolved, none deferred. Three decision-lane calls ratified by chat directive after real discussion — the empty-domain one survived two rounds of pushback that made the finding stronger rather than dismissing it, and it reversed my own prior recommendation. The two WARNINGs both traded a cheap record for a real shape change, and the walk deliberately split on which deserved which: the taxonomy is the product's contract, the passed/unverified distinction is what the summary is allowed to claim. No behaviour regressions: 2200 tests green, validate --all --strict clean, base fingerprint verified, marker sweep zero, and the no-registry path re-verified byte-identical against the pre-change HEAD build.
